{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mt-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"aaa921fc46b15266f9a1f158a846f6c747f693803341125c4548b14e9ef221ed","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mt-class-d:lineage:1","source_registry_sha256":"35425fc1b75886d4bce9129f5de9443ae8cee634cff4a62363bbcd7cc017fe32","source_liveness_sha256":"bf7b5d7e97593e3a1c6181f4785c9171cedac6e24ab65da907a644a4b4907add"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Licensing and required documents","heading":"C2 — Licensing and required documents","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Licensing and required documents

FACT_ID: sec01-R01 | anchor: A01
A valid, unexpired Northern Mariana I-551 card marked Northern Mariana rather than permanent resident is accepted for authorized-presence proof. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R02 | anchor: A01
A valid, unexpired American Indian I-551 card marked American Indian rather than permanent resident is accepted for authorized-presence proof. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R03 | anchor: A01
Authorized presence may be established with a valid, unexpired United States citizen identification card on form I-179 or I-197. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R04 | anchor: A01
A valid, unexpired permanent resident card on form I-551 is accepted as authorized-presence evidence. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec01-R05 | anchor: A02
An unexpired, valid temporary resident identification card on form I-688 is accepted for authorized-presence proof. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R06 | anchor: A02
A valid, unexpired United States re-entry permit on form I-327 may establish authorized presence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R07 | anchor: A02
A valid, unexpired refugee travel document on form I-571 may establish authorized presence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R08 | anchor: A02
Authorized-presence proof may use a valid, unexpired employment authorization card on form I-688A, I-688B or I-766. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R09 | anchor: A02
A valid, unexpired I-94 arrival-and-departure record marked refugee can establish authorized presence without a valid passport when it has the refugee stamp and an attached photo. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R10 | anchor: A02
A digital identification card from a federally recognized tribe whose reservation is in Montana can prove authorized presence if it includes the applicant’s digitized image, birth date and tribal enrollment number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R11 | anchor: A02
To establish full legal name and birth date, an applicant needs either two primary documents or a primary document together with a secondary document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R12 | anchor: A02
A color-photo driver license or identification card from a United States or Canadian jurisdiction is primary identity evidence if it has not been expired for more than four years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R13 | anchor: A02
A certified birth certificate from a United States or Canadian jurisdiction qualifies as a primary identity document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R14 | anchor: A02
A State Department or United States embassy birth-abroad certification on form FS-240 or DS-1350 is primary identity evidence for a United States citizen. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R15 | anchor: A02
A federally recognized Indian tribe’s digital card is primary identity evidence when its reservation is in Montana and the card includes the applicant’s image, birth date and enrollment number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R16 | anchor: A02
An unexpired Defense Department military identification card can serve as primary identity evidence for active-duty, reserve, retired personnel or active-duty dependents when it displays the applicant’s color photo or digital image and birth date. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R17 | anchor: A02
A current United States State Department passport or passport card is acceptable primary identity evidence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R18 | anchor: A02
A valid, unexpired foreign passport is primary identity evidence with a same-name I-94 bearing an unexpired nonimmigrant endorsement, or an unexpired permanent-resident I-551 stamp. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R19 | anchor: A02
The listed valid, unexpired USCIS naturalization certificates N-550, N-570 and N-578 qualify as primary identity evidence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R20 | anchor: A02
Primary identity evidence includes valid, unexpired USCIS citizenship certificates N-560, N-561 and N-645. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R21 | anchor: A02
The listed valid, unexpired USCIS Northern Mariana or American Indian I-551 cards require their respective special imprint to qualify as primary identity evidence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R22 | anchor: A02
A valid, unexpired USCIS citizen identification card I-179 or I-197, or permanent resident card I-551, qualifies as primary identity evidence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R23 | anchor: A02
Primary identity evidence can include the listed valid, unexpired USCIS temporary resident card I-688, re-entry permit I-327, refugee travel document I-571 or employment card I-688A, I-688B or I-766. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R24 | anchor: A02
A valid, unexpired USCIS I-94 refugee record without a valid passport qualifies as primary identity evidence when marked refugee and carrying an affixed photo. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R25 | anchor: A02
A current United States or Canadian instruction permit, learner permit or license-or-permit receipt qualifies as primary identity evidence if it shows the applicant’s photo and birth date. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R26 | anchor: A02
A Montana Department of Corrections inmate identification card is primary identity evidence when it includes the applicant’s photo or digitized image, birth date and adult offender number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R27 | anchor: A02
A driver-licensing authority’s certified emergency photo identification from a United States or Canadian jurisdiction must show name and birth date and is not accepted for mailed renewals or mailed duplicates. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R28 | anchor: A02
A second primary identity document can be used as the secondary document. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec01-R29 | anchor: A03
An original United States Social Security card or Canadian social insurance card qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R30 | anchor: A03
A government-issued certified marriage certificate or marriage license qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R31 | anchor: A03
A United States or Canadian driver license or identification card expired for over one year but no more than five years can be secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R32 | anchor: A03
A current photo identification card for a United States or Canadian government employee qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R33 | anchor: A03
A current United States or Canadian driver license or identification card without a color photo may serve as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R34 | anchor: A03
A competent United States or Canadian court’s certified order or judgment showing the applicant’s full legal name and birth date qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R35 | anchor: A03
A USCIS document otherwise approved as primary evidence may be secondary evidence when it has been expired for no more than one year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R36 | anchor: A03
A certified birth certificate from outside the listed United States jurisdictions and Canadian provinces or territories may serve as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R37 | anchor: A03
A Defense Department certification of release or discharge qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R38 | anchor: A03
A Medicare, Medicaid or health-insurance card can be secondary identity evidence if it shows the applicant’s name and individual program or insurance number. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R39 | anchor: A03
An unexpired color-photo firearm or concealed-weapon permit qualifies as secondary identity evidence if issued by a full-time organized police department’s chief or a United States local county sheriff. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R40 | anchor: A03
A current Federal Aviation Administration pilot license is acceptable secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R41 | anchor: A03
Certified records or a transcript from an elementary, secondary or postsecondary school qualify as secondary identity evidence when they show the applicant’s full name, preferably with birth date. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R42 | anchor: A03
A Montana-approved driver or traffic education completion certificate showing the applicant’s name and birth date qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R43 | anchor: A03
A current school photo identification card showing the student’s name and student identification number qualifies as secondary identity evidence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R44 | anchor: A03
A certified child’s birth certificate, or a fax or photocopy of that certified copy, can be secondary identity evidence if it lists the applicant as parent with name and birth date. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R45 | anchor: A03
Original license applicants must prove their Montana residence address and also give a mailing address if they cannot receive mail at the residence. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R46 | anchor: A03
A residence-evidence document must show the applicant’s name and Montana residence address as entered on the license application. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R47 | anchor: A03
The handbook accepts a listed primary or secondary identity document, the previous year’s United States or Montana income-tax return, or a Montana voter registration card as residence evidence when the required name and address appear. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R48 | anchor: A03
Residence evidence may use a Montana state-or-county property-tax receipt from the last year or a current automobile or life-insurance policy or statement, with the applicant’s name and residential address. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R49 | anchor: A03
Certified school records can prove residence when the applicant attends or attended the issuing school within four months of the application and the name and residence address are shown. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R50 | anchor: A03
A parent, guardian, responsible adult or adult child may confirm shared residence in writing if a permitted address document for that person is also supplied. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R51 | anchor: A03
An original landlord-signed or rental-agent-signed rental agreement or rent receipt can prove residence when it includes the applicant’s name and residential address. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R52 | anchor: A03
Mortgage or home-equity papers can establish residence when they show the applicant’s name and address, with a rural address accepted if no other physical address exists. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R53 | anchor: A03
A payroll check or stub, bank statement, utility bill or hookup order, or canceled mail can prove residence when dated or issued within four months before application and showing the applicant’s name and residential address. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R54 | anchor: A03
A homeless applicant must give a descriptive location address and separate mailing address, plus a social-service agency’s letterhead statement verifying homelessness and that location. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec01-R55 | anchor: A04
REAL ID applicants must provide unaltered required documents for each required step, with agency certification or MVD verification where required. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R56 | anchor: A04
The REAL ID identity step requires proof of current legal name, birth date and United States citizenship or other lawful federal authorization to be present. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R57 | anchor: A04
For REAL ID, proof of an issued Social Security number must show the applicant’s name and full number, which is checked with the Social Security Administration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R58 | anchor: A04
REAL ID residence proof requires two acceptable documents bearing the applicant’s name and current physical address; they must be unexpired or within one year of expiration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R59 | anchor: A04
REAL ID residency documents may be of the same type. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec01-R60 | anchor: A04
When the current legal name differs from the identity or Social Security documents, a REAL ID applicant must document every legal name change back to the original documented name. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0017]
